title: In FlyWire v783, 6.9 percent of selected reciprocal pairs retain five contacts per direction after any one neuropil loss
abstract: We tested whether reciprocal contacts in FlyWire release 783 retain a count threshold after loss of any one neuropil. An exact count rule uses the total in each direction minus its largest regional count. Of 188,724 pairs with at least five contacts per direction, 12,955 (6.86 percent) pass. After coarse control for directional counts and dominant regions, acetylcholine-GABA pairs had a standardized safe rate of 1.02 percent, compared with 1.68 percent for acetylcholine-acetylcholine pairs. The difference was -0.657 percentage points, with a cell-weighting interval of -0.983 to -0.326. The package gives code, hashes, a full derived pair table, deletion checks, and threshold tests. One fly, predicted transmitter labels, atlas compartments, coarse matching, and no matched activity limit the result. Count survival does not establish physiological feedback survival.

display.caption: The left panel shows exact safe shares at four contact thresholds. Each threshold selects a different set of pairs. The right panel compares raw shares and common-stratum standardized shares at five contacts. Safety means retention of the required count in both directions after any one neuropil is removed.
